[TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/29 (Mon) 13:38  
[USER] User inquired about how a trustee handles conflicts of interest that may arise between themselves and beneficiaries of the trust.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] A trustee is obligated to act in the best interests of the beneficiaries and must avoid any conflicts of interest.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] If a conflict of interest arises, the trustee must disclose the conflict to the beneficiaries and seek their informed consent before making any decisions.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] If the conflict cannot be resolved, the trustee may have to resign from the trust.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Trustees can seek guidance from legal and financial professionals to ensure they are fulfilling their fiduciary duties properly.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The trustee's actions should be transparent and in the best interests of the beneficiaries.  
[USER] User requested an example of a conflict of interest that a trustee may face.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Example of a conflict of interest: A trustee who is also a beneficiary may want to make a decision that benefits themselves but not necessarily in the best interest of other beneficiaries.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The trustee may want to invest trust funds in a business venture in which they have a personal interest, even if it may not be the best investment for the trust as a whole.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] In such a scenario, the trustee must disclose the conflict and get approval from all the beneficiaries affected by the decision.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] If the conflict can't be resolved, the trustee may need to resign from their position.  
[USER] User acknowledged the importance of transparency in handling conflicts of interest and asked if there is anything else a trustee should keep in mind to fulfill their fiduciary duties properly.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Transparency is crucial when handling conflicts of interest as a trustee.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Other principles a trustee should keep in mind include:  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 1. Loyalty: A trustee should put the interests of the beneficiaries ahead of their own interests.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 2. Prudence: A trustee should use reasonable care and good judgment when making investment decisions and managing the trust property.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 3. Impartiality: A trustee should treat all beneficiaries impartially and not favor one beneficiary over another.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 4. Communication: A trustee should keep beneficiaries informed about the trust and any significant decisions or changes.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 5. Record-keeping: A trustee should maintain accurate and complete records of all transactions involving the trust.
